title: Treasury Secretary Bessent Moves to Military Base After Iran-Linked Threats
dek: Scott Bessent has moved from his home in the Washington area to a military base after threats against his life that officials and reporters tie to Iran.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: The U.S. Treasury Department building in Washington

keyPoints: The New York Times first reported that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has relocated from his home to a military base, citing three people with knowledge of the matter.
CBS News reported that the move followed a Wall Street Journal article with an online photo that made the location of Bessent’s Georgetown home identifiable.
A Treasury spokesperson said Bessent “will not be deterred” by the Iranian regime’s threats and remains committed to the blockade and sanctions campaign against Iran.
The exact nature and severity of the threats have not been made public, the BBC reported.
body:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has moved from his home in the Washington area to a military base after a series of Iran-linked threats against his life, according to reporting by the [New York Times](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/10/us/politics/bessent-moved-base-iran-threats.html), [CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/bessent-relocate-dc-area-home-military-base-iran-threats-to-kill-him/) and the [BBC](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cqr7gr0010r2o). The Associated Press also reported that Bessent was recently forced to relocate over concerns for his safety.

## What the reports say

The New York Times reported the move first, citing three people with knowledge of the matter. CBS News said a source pointed to a Wall Street Journal article that included an online photo of Bessent’s Georgetown home, which the source said allowed the house to be geo-located and raised security concerns. The BBC, which cited CBS as its U.S. partner, reported the same sequence.

## The Treasury response

A Treasury Department spokesperson said Bessent “will not be deterred by the Iranian regime’s threats” and “remains committed to executing Operation Economic Outcast and maintaining the blockade, which together are collapsing Iran’s economy,” CBS News reported. The BBC reported that the exact nature and severity of the threats remain unclear.

## Wider context

Bessent has led the administration’s effort to isolate Iran economically through sanctions and a naval blockade. The BBC reported that U.S. intelligence has warned Iran has “substantially increased” efforts to target Americans, including U.S. officials. Citing the New York Times, the BBC said the effort includes current and former officials, and listed former Secretary of State Mike Pompeo, former national security adviser John Bolton and former Joint Chiefs chairman Mark Milley among officials reportedly on Iran’s list of potential targets.

The BBC also noted that several administration officials live on military bases, including Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Secretary of State Marco Rubio. The reports reviewed by Meridian do not include a White House response to requests for comment.
